scenario: A startup wants to avoid buying servers up front and pay only for the computing it uses. Which cloud benefit is this?

options.text: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Go global in minutes with Regions

explanation: Swapping up-front hardware purchases (capital expense) for pay-as-you-go spending (variable expense) is the first of the six advantages of cloud computing. The other options describe capacity, reach or speed, not how you pay.

refs.title: Six advantages of cloud computing - Overview of Amazon Web Services

scenario: A retailer's traffic spikes every holiday season. Which cloud benefit lets it avoid buying servers for peak load all year?

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale

options.note: Related, but the question is about sizing.

explanation: Provision for the actual need and scale out for the holiday peak, then scale back in. This is 'stop guessing capacity', because you no longer buy for the peak and leave it idle the rest of the year.

refs.title: Six advantages of cloud computing - Overview of Amazon Web Services

scenario: Why can AWS often offer lower prices than a company running its own data center?

options.note: Data transfer out is usually charged.

explanation: Because AWS aggregates usage from a huge number of customers, it buys and runs hardware at lower cost per unit and passes savings on. Data transfer out is not free, and nothing is unlimited and free.

refs.title: Six advantages of cloud computing - Overview of Amazon Web Services

scenario: A company wants to launch its app for customers in Asia without building new data centers. Which benefit applies?
explanation: Deploying into AWS Regions around the world takes minutes, so a company can serve Asian customers with low latency without building data centers. This is 'go global in minutes'.

refs.title: Six advantages of cloud computing - Overview of Amazon Web Services
AWS Global Infrastructure: Regions and Availability Zones

scenario: Which describes elasticity in the cloud?

options.text: Automatically adding and removing resources to match demand
Keeping copies of data in three separate locations
Paying for capacity in advance to get a discount

explanation: Elasticity means resources are added and removed automatically as demand changes, so you match capacity to load. Copies in several locations is durability, and prepaying is a pricing commitment.

refs.title: Six advantages of cloud computing - Overview of Amazon Web Services
What is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling?

scenario: Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focuses on recovering from failures and meeting demand?
explanation: Reliability covers recovering from failures and meeting demand. The pillar also includes testing recovery procedures and scaling horizontally. Performance efficiency is about using resources well, not recovering.

refs.title: The pillars of the framework - AWS Well-Architected Framework

scenario: Which Well-Architected pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impact of workloads?
explanation: Sustainability is the Well-Architected pillar about minimizing environmental impact. The six pillars are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability.

refs.title: The pillars of the framework - AWS Well-Architected Framework

scenario: Which Well-Architected pillar includes running workloads, monitoring them and making small, frequent, reversible changes?
explanation: Operational excellence covers running and monitoring workloads, performing operations as code and making small, frequent, reversible changes, then learning from failures. Cost and performance pillars don't address that.

refs.title: The pillars of the framework - AWS Well-Architected Framework

scenario: A team selects the right EC2 instance types and uses caching to meet latency goals. Which Well-Architected pillar is this?
explanation: Choosing appropriate instance types and adding caching to meet latency goals is the performance efficiency pillar: using computing resources efficiently as demand and technology change.

refs.title: The pillars of the framework - AWS Well-Architected Framework

scenario: Which Well-Architected pillar includes analyzing spending and removing unused resources?
explanation: Cost optimization covers analyzing spend, adopting a consumption model and removing unused resources. Reliability and performance efficiency don't focus on spending.

refs.title: The pillars of the framework - AWS Well-Architected Framework

scenario: Which tool reviews a workload against AWS best practices and highlights high-risk issues?
explanation: The AWS Well-Architected Tool reviews a workload against the framework's questions and flags high-risk issues; it's free in the console. Pricing Calculator estimates cost, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities and Artifact provides compliance reports.

refs.title: The pillars of the framework - AWS Well-Architected Framework

scenario: Which design principle recommends building systems that keep working if one component fails?
explanation: 'Design for failure' means assuming components will fail and building so the system keeps working: multiple AZs, loose coupling and automatic recovery. A single large server or one AZ is a single point of failure.

refs.title: The pillars of the framework - AWS Well-Architected Framework
AWS Global Infrastructure: Regions and Availability Zones

scenario: Which principle describes breaking an application into components that communicate through queues so one failure doesn't stop the others?

options.note: Components depend directly on each other.

explanation: Loose coupling lets components communicate through intermediaries such as Amazon SQS queues, so a failure or slowdown in one component doesn't stop the others. Tight coupling is the opposite.

refs.title: What is Amazon Simple Queue Service?
The pillars of the framework - AWS Well-Architected Framework

scenario: Which migration strategy moves an application to AWS without changes?

options.note: Moves to a different product, like SaaS.

explanation: Rehost ('lift and shift') moves an application to AWS as-is, with no changes. Refactor changes the architecture, repurchase moves to a different product, and retire turns the app off.

refs.title: About the migration strategies - AWS Prescriptive Guidance

scenario: A company moves its database to Amazon RDS with minor changes, but doesn't redesign the app. Which strategy is this?
explanation: Moving the database to Amazon RDS with only minor changes, without redesigning the app, is replatform ('lift, tinker and shift'). Rehost has no changes at all, and refactor re-architects.

refs.title: About the migration strategies - AWS Prescriptive Guidance
What is Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)?

scenario: A company replaces its on-premises CRM with a SaaS product. Which migration strategy is this?

options.note: Small changes to the same app.

explanation: Replacing an on-premises CRM with a SaaS product is repurchase: moving to a different product, often a SaaS license, rather than moving the existing software.

refs.title: About the migration strategies - AWS Prescriptive Guidance

scenario: A company decides to keep some apps in its data center for now because they're not ready to move. Which strategy is this?
explanation: Retain means leaving workloads where they are for now because they aren't ready to move, and revisiting later. Retire decommissions the app instead.

refs.title: About the migration strategies - AWS Prescriptive Guidance

scenario: A company redesigns a monolithic app into serverless microservices. Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Rebuilding a monolith as serverless microservices is refactor (re-architect): the most effort, but the largest cloud benefits. Rehost and repurchase leave the design essentially unchanged.

refs.title: About the migration strategies - AWS Prescriptive Guidance

scenario: Which framework helps organizations plan their cloud adoption across perspectives like Business, People and Governance?
explanation: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) organizes cloud adoption guidance into perspectives such as Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security and Operations. Well-Architected reviews workload designs instead.

refs.title: An Overview of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework

scenario: Which AWS CAF perspective focuses on culture, training and organizational change?
explanation: The People perspective covers culture, training and organizational change. Platform, Operations and Security are the technical perspectives.

refs.title: An Overview of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework

scenario: Which AWS CAF perspective focuses on building the cloud architecture and infrastructure?
explanation: The Platform perspective covers building the cloud architecture and infrastructure. Business, People and Governance focus on business capabilities.

refs.title: An Overview of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework

scenario: Which is a benefit of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework?

options.text: Free EC2 instances for a year

options.note: CAF is guidance, not a tool.

explanation: AWS CAF helps lower business risk, improve ESG performance, grow revenue and increase operational efficiency. It does not provide free instances, automatic code migration or unlimited support.

refs.title: An Overview of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework

scenario: Which service helps move on-premises servers to AWS by continuously replicating them?
explanation: AWS Application Migration Service continuously replicates on-premises servers to AWS so you can cut over with little downtime, the main tool for rehosting. DMS is for databases and Artifact for compliance reports.

refs.title: About the migration strategies - AWS Prescriptive Guidance

scenario: Which service migrates a database to AWS while the source stays operational?
explanation: AWS Database Migration Service migrates databases while the source stays operational, including between different engines (with Schema Conversion). DataSync moves files, and Backup protects data.

refs.title: What is AWS Database Migration Service?

scenario: Which concept means a company only pays for compute while its code actually runs?

options.note: Pay for a whole physical server.

explanation: Serverless computing, such as AWS Lambda, charges only for requests and execution time, so you pay for compute only while code runs. Reserved Instances and Dedicated Hosts bill whether or not they are busy.

refs.title: Types of cloud computing - Overview of Amazon Web Services

scenario: Which deployment model connects on-premises infrastructure with cloud resources?

options.note: Multiple AWS Regions, not on premises.

explanation: Hybrid cloud connects on-premises infrastructure with cloud resources, using services such as Outposts, Direct Connect and Site-to-Site VPN. Multi-Region is still all cloud.

refs.title: Types of cloud computing - Overview of Amazon Web Services

scenario: Which is an advantage of the cloud's economies of scale for customers?
explanation: Economies of scale let AWS lower its pay-as-you-go prices as it grows, and it has done so many times. It doesn't remove security responsibilities or the need for connectivity.

refs.title: Six advantages of cloud computing - Overview of Amazon Web Services

scenario: A company wants to experiment with new ideas quickly and shut down failed experiments at low cost. Which benefit applies?
explanation: Because resources are a click or API call away, teams can try ideas and shut down failures cheaply. That's 'increase speed and agility', not durability or global reach.

refs.title: Six advantages of cloud computing - Overview of Amazon Web Services

scenario: Which describes the cloud's total cost of ownership (TCO) advantage?

options.text: Lower costs for hardware, power and staff
Free software licenses for all apps

explanation: Total cost of ownership compares all costs of running IT: hardware, power, cooling, space and labor. The cloud lowers those costs; it doesn't make software, storage or taxes free.

refs.title: Six advantages of cloud computing - Overview of Amazon Web Services

scenario: Under the shared responsibility model, which task is the customer's responsibility for Amazon EC2?
explanation: For EC2 the customer secures what's in the cloud: the guest OS, applications, security groups and data. AWS secures the physical servers, data center and hypervisor.

scenario: Under the shared responsibility model, which is AWS's responsibility?
explanation: AWS is responsible for security of the cloud, including the physical security of data centers, hardware, networking and the facilities behind the services. Security groups, encryption choices and IAM users are the customer's.

scenario: Which is a shared control between AWS and the customer?
explanation: Patch management is shared: AWS patches the infrastructure and customers patch their guest OS and applications. Physical security and data center power are AWS-only, and access decisions are the customer's.

scenario: For a managed service like Amazon RDS, who patches the database engine?

options.note: Patching is part of the service.

explanation: Amazon RDS is managed, so AWS patches the database engine and the underlying OS. The customer still controls access, data and configuration. More managed services mean more AWS responsibility.

refs.title: What is Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)?

scenario: Which AWS account identity has complete access and should be used only for a few account tasks?
explanation: The root user has complete access to the account, so it's reserved for the few tasks that require it. Use IAM users, roles or IAM Identity Center for everyday work.

scenario: What is the best practice for protecting the root user?

options.text: Enable MFA and lock away its credentials
Share it with the whole admin team
Create long-term access keys for it

explanation: Protect the root user with MFA and keep its credentials locked away, and don't create access keys for it. Sharing it or using it daily defeats its purpose.

scenario: Which task requires signing in as the root user?
explanation: Closing the AWS account requires signing in as the root user. Launching EC2 instances, creating buckets and viewing metrics are done with IAM identities.

scenario: Which principle grants users only the permissions they need to do their job?
explanation: Least privilege grants only the permissions needed to do a job. Start minimal and add as required. Defense in depth is layered controls, not permission scope.

scenario: An EC2 instance needs to read objects from S3. What's the most secure way to give it access?

options.text: Attach an IAM role to the instance
Store access keys on the instance

explanation: Attach an IAM role to the instance. It provides temporary credentials that rotate automatically, so no access keys live on the instance. Public buckets and root keys are insecure.

refs.title: Use an IAM role to grant permissions to applications running on Amazon EC2 instances

scenario: Which IAM feature groups users so they share the same permissions?

options.note: Assumed temporarily, not a collection of users.

explanation: IAM groups let users share permissions: attach a policy to the group rather than to each user. Roles are assumed temporarily and security groups are network firewalls.

scenario: Which document defines permissions in IAM?
explanation: IAM permissions are defined in JSON policy documents with Effect, Action, Resource and optional Conditions. CloudFormation templates and security group rules are different things.

scenario: Which service provides single sign-on to multiple AWS accounts and business apps for a workforce?
explanation: IAM Identity Center provides single sign-on to multiple AWS accounts and business apps for the workforce, and can connect to an external identity provider such as Microsoft Entra ID. Cognito is for customer-facing apps.

scenario: Which service adds sign-up and sign-in to a customer-facing mobile app?
explanation: Amazon Cognito adds sign-up and sign-in to customer-facing apps, with user pools and social sign-in. IAM Identity Center is for your workforce.

scenario: A company with many AWS accounts wants to block all accounts from using certain Regions. What should it use?

options.text: Service control policies in AWS Organizations
IAM user policies in each account

explanation: Service control policies in AWS Organizations set the maximum permissions for member accounts, so a Region-deny SCP applies across all accounts. Per-account IAM policies or security groups can't do this centrally.

scenario: Where can a customer download AWS compliance reports such as SOC and ISO certifications?
explanation: AWS Artifact is the portal for compliance reports (SOC, ISO) and for reviewing and accepting agreements such as a BAA. CloudTrail and Config record account activity, not auditor reports.

scenario: Which service records API calls made in an AWS account for auditing?
explanation: CloudTrail records API calls and account activity, answering who did what, when and from where. CloudWatch collects metrics and logs, and Config tracks resource configuration.

scenario: Which service tracks resource configuration changes and checks them against rules?
explanation: AWS Config records resource configuration changes over time and evaluates them against rules, such as flagging unencrypted volumes. CloudTrail records API calls instead.

scenario: Which service uses machine learning to detect threats like unusual API calls or compromised instances?
explanation: Amazon GuardDuty uses machine learning and threat intelligence on CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs to detect threats such as unusual API calls and compromised instances.

scenario: Which service automatically scans EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities?
explanation: Amazon Inspector continuously scans EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities. GuardDuty detects threats and Macie finds sensitive data.

scenario: Which service discovers personally identifiable information (PII) stored in Amazon S3?
explanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover sensitive data such as PII in Amazon S3. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, not data content.

scenario: Which service gives a combined view of security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector and Macie?
explanation: AWS Security Hub aggregates findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie and other services into one view and runs automated best-practice checks.

refs.title: Introduction to AWS Security Hub CSPM

scenario: Which service helps investigate the root cause of a security finding using graphs of related activity?
explanation: Amazon Detective builds linked graphs from logs so you can investigate the root cause of a security finding. Inspector, WAF and KMS don't do investigations.

scenario: Which service protects all AWS customers from common DDoS attacks at no extra cost?

options.note: Paid, with extra protections and response team.

explanation: AWS Shield Standard automatically protects all customers from common DDoS attacks at no extra cost. Shield Advanced is the paid tier with extra protection and response support.

scenario: A company wants to block SQL injection and cross-site scripting requests to its web app. What should it use?
explanation: AWS WAF filters web requests, blocking SQL injection and cross-site scripting, and works with CloudFront, Application Load Balancer and API Gateway. Shield addresses DDoS instead.

scenario: Which service creates and manages encryption keys used by many AWS services?
explanation: AWS KMS creates and manages encryption keys used by many AWS services. CloudHSM gives dedicated hardware modules, and Secrets Manager stores secrets, not keys.

scenario: Which service stores database passwords and can rotate them automatically?
explanation: AWS Secrets Manager stores credentials such as database passwords and can rotate them automatically. KMS manages encryption keys, not stored secrets.

scenario: Which service provides free public TLS certificates for use with load balancers and CloudFront?
explanation: AWS Certificate Manager provisions free public TLS certificates for integrated services such as load balancers and CloudFront, and renews them automatically.

scenario: Which acts as a stateful firewall for an EC2 instance?

options.note: Connects a VPC to the internet.

explanation: A security group is a stateful firewall for an instance: it has allow rules only, and return traffic is allowed automatically. A network ACL is stateless and applies to subnets.

refs.title: Control traffic to your AWS resources using security groups
Control subnet traffic with network access control lists

scenario: Which is true of network ACLs?

options.text: They're stateless and apply to subnets
They're stateful and apply to instances

explanation: Network ACLs are stateless and apply at the subnet level, so return traffic must be explicitly allowed. Security groups are the stateful, instance-level control. NACLs can allow and deny.

refs.title: Control subnet traffic with network access control lists
Control traffic to your AWS resources using security groups

scenario: Who is responsible for encrypting data stored in Amazon S3 for a specific compliance need?

options.note: AWS provides tools; customers choose settings.

explanation: Encryption choices for data in S3 belong to the customer. S3 encrypts new objects by default, but customers decide on key management to meet their compliance needs.

scenario: Which describes data encryption in transit?

options.text: Protecting data as it moves over a network
Protecting data stored on a disk
Copying data to another Region for backup

explanation: Encryption in transit protects data moving across a network, commonly with TLS (HTTPS). Encryption at rest protects stored data.

scenario: What's the main benefit of requiring multi-factor authentication (MFA) in AWS?

options.text: Stolen passwords alone can't sign in
Users no longer need any passwords
It encrypts all data stored in S3

explanation: MFA adds a second factor, so a stolen password alone can't sign in. It does not replace passwords or encrypt S3 data. Use authenticator apps, passkeys or hardware keys.

scenario: Which IAM tool shows when a user's credentials were last used, to help remove unused ones?
explanation: The IAM credential report lists users and when their passwords and access keys were last used, helping you remove unused credentials. Cost Explorer and Artifact aren't about credentials.

refs.title: Generate credential reports for your AWS account

scenario: Which service sends alerts when a CloudWatch metric crosses a threshold, such as high CPU?
explanation: CloudWatch alarms watch a metric and act when it crosses a threshold, sending notifications through SNS or triggering Auto Scaling. CloudTrail trails record API activity, not metric thresholds.

scenario: Which service provides managed Microsoft Active Directory in AWS?
explanation: AWS Directory Service provides managed Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD) that can trust an on-premises domain. Cognito is for app users, IAM for AWS permissions.

scenario: What is an AWS Region?

options.text: A geographic area with multiple Availability Zones

options.note: That's closer to an AZ's building.

options.text: A cache location for the CDN network

explanation: A Region is a geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones. Choose Regions by compliance, latency, service availability and price. An edge location is not a Region.

refs.title: AWS Global Infrastructure: Regions and Availability Zones

scenario: What is an Availability Zone?

options.text: One or more data centers with separate power and networking
A caching site used by CloudFront

explanation: An Availability Zone is one or more data centers with independent power and networking, connected by low-latency links but isolated from each other's failures.

refs.title: AWS Global Infrastructure: Regions and Availability Zones

scenario: How can an application be made highly available within a Region?

options.text: Deploy it across multiple Availability Zones
Use a single, larger EC2 instance
options.note: Still a single point of failure.

options.text: Use one AZ with nightly backups

explanation: Deploy across multiple Availability Zones behind a load balancer so one AZ failure doesn't stop the app. A bigger instance or a single AZ remains a single point of failure.

refs.title: AWS Global Infrastructure: Regions and Availability Zones

scenario: Which factor is NOT usually a reason for choosing an AWS Region?

options.text: The number of IAM users needed

explanation: Region choice depends on data residency, latency, service availability and price. The number of IAM users doesn't matter because IAM is global.

refs.title: AWS Global Infrastructure: Regions and Availability Zones

scenario: What are edge locations used for?
explanation: Edge locations cache content closer to users and are used by CloudFront, Route 53 and Global Accelerator. RDS and EBS run in Regions and AZs, not at the edge.

refs.title: AWS Global Infrastructure: Regions and Availability Zones

scenario: Which service runs AWS infrastructure in a customer's own data center?
explanation: AWS Outposts puts AWS infrastructure and services in the customer's own data center, for low latency or data residency. Local Zones are AWS-operated metro extensions.

scenario: Which AWS infrastructure places compute close to large cities for single-digit millisecond latency?
explanation: AWS Local Zones place compute and storage near large cities for single-digit millisecond latency, extending a parent Region. Outposts sits in the customer's own facility.

scenario: Which service provides resizable virtual servers in the cloud?
explanation: Amazon EC2 provides resizable virtual servers. Pick an instance family (general purpose, compute, memory, storage or accelerated) to fit the workload. S3 is storage and Lambda is serverless.

scenario: Which service runs code without servers in response to events, billed per request and duration?
explanation: AWS Lambda runs code in response to events without servers, billed for requests and duration. Functions can run for up to 15 minutes. EC2 and Lightsail use servers you manage.

scenario: Which service runs containers without managing servers or clusters of EC2 instances?
explanation: AWS Fargate runs containers without managing servers or EC2 clusters, and works with both ECS and EKS. EC2 Auto Scaling and Batch on EC2 still involve instances.

refs.title: Architect for AWS Fargate for Amazon ECS

scenario: Which service runs Kubernetes clusters managed by AWS?
explanation: Amazon EKS is managed Kubernetes. Amazon ECS is AWS's own container orchestrator and ECR stores container images.

scenario: A developer wants to upload code and have AWS handle deployment, load balancing and scaling. Which service fits?
explanation: Elastic Beanstalk lets developers upload code while AWS handles provisioning, load balancing and scaling, and you can still control the underlying resources. CloudFormation requires you to define resources.

scenario: Which service offers simple virtual servers with a predictable monthly price for small websites?
explanation: Amazon Lightsail bundles compute, storage and data transfer in simple virtual servers with a predictable monthly price, suited to small websites and apps.

scenario: Which service automatically adds or removes EC2 instances based on demand?
explanation: EC2 Auto Scaling adds or removes instances based on demand and replaces unhealthy ones. Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic but doesn't change the number of instances.

refs.title: What is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling?

scenario: Which service distributes incoming traffic across multiple EC2 instances?
explanation: Elastic Load Balancing spreads incoming traffic across multiple targets. Application Load Balancers route HTTP/HTTPS and Network Load Balancers handle TCP/UDP. Route 53 is DNS.

scenario: Which storage service stores any amount of data as objects in buckets?
explanation: Amazon S3 is object storage: unlimited objects in buckets, designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability. EBS is block storage and EFS is a shared file system.

scenario: Which S3 storage class is lowest cost for archives that are rarely accessed and can wait hours to retrieve?
explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class for rarely accessed archives, with retrievals taking hours (typically within 12 hours, up to 48 for bulk). Standard and Standard-IA cost more.

refs.title: Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes

scenario: A company has data with unknown or changing access patterns. Which S3 class moves data automatically to save cost?
explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between access tiers automatically as access patterns change, with no retrieval fees, ideal for unknown or changing patterns. One Zone-IA and Glacier aren't automatic.

refs.title: Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes

scenario: Which storage is a block-level volume attached to a single EC2 instance and persists after stopping it?
explanation: Amazon EBS provides block-level volumes for a single EC2 instance that persist after the instance stops. Instance store is lost on stop, and EBS volumes live in one AZ; snapshots back them up.

refs.title: What is Amazon Elastic Block Store?

scenario: Which storage provides a shared file system that many Linux EC2 instances can mount at once?
explanation: Amazon EFS is a shared file system that many Linux instances can mount at the same time. EBS attaches to one instance. FSx offers Windows File Server, Lustre and others.

refs.title: What is Amazon Elastic File System?

scenario: Which service connects on-premises applications to cloud storage using a local appliance or VM?
explanation: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises applications to cloud storage through a local appliance or VM, in File, Volume and Tape Gateway modes. EFS and CloudFront don't bridge on-premises storage.

scenario: Which service centrally manages and automates backups across AWS services?
explanation: AWS Backup centrally manages and automates backups across AWS services through backup plans with schedules and retention. Storage Gateway and DataSync move data instead.

scenario: Which managed relational database service supports engines like MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server?
explanation: Amazon RDS is the managed relational database service supporting engines such as MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server. Multi-AZ adds a standby for availability. DynamoDB is NoSQL.

refs.title: What is Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)?

scenario: Which AWS-built relational database is compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL and offers higher performance?
explanation: Amazon Aurora is AWS's MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database with higher performance, storing six copies of data across three AZs. DynamoDB and Neptune are not relational MySQL-compatible.

scenario: Which serverless NoSQL database provides single-digit millisecond performance at any scale?
explanation: DynamoDB is a serverless key-value and document NoSQL database with single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. RDS and Aurora are relational, and Redshift is a data warehouse.

scenario: Which service is a data warehouse for running analytics queries on large datasets?
explanation: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics queries on large datasets, with a serverless option. DynamoDB and ElastiCache serve operational workloads.

scenario: Which service adds an in-memory cache to speed up database reads?
explanation: Amazon ElastiCache adds an in-memory cache (Valkey, Redis OSS or Memcached) in front of a database to speed up reads. S3 and Backup don't cache queries.

scenario: Which service creates a logically isolated virtual network in AWS?
explanation: Amazon VPC provides a logically isolated virtual network with subnets, route tables and gateways. Direct Connect, Route 53 and Global Accelerator are connectivity, DNS and routing services.

scenario: Which component lets resources in a public subnet reach the internet?
explanation: An internet gateway lets resources in a public subnet reach the internet; a route to it makes the subnet public. A NAT gateway serves private subnets outbound only.

refs.title: Enable internet access for a VPC using an internet gateway

scenario: Which service provides a dedicated private network connection from on premises to AWS?
explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private network connection from on premises to AWS with consistent performance. Site-to-Site VPN is faster to set up but uses the internet.

scenario: Which service is a scalable DNS service that can route users based on latency or health?
explanation: Amazon Route 53 is a scalable DNS service whose routing policies include simple, weighted, latency, failover and geolocation, with health checks. CloudFront is a content delivery network.

scenario: Which service delivers website content with low latency using a global network of edge locations?
explanation: Amazon CloudFront delivers content with low latency through a global network of edge locations, serving S3, load balancers or other origins. Route 53 resolves DNS names.

scenario: Which service decouples application components using a message queue?
explanation: Amazon SQS is a message queue that decouples components: messages wait until a consumer processes them. SNS pushes to many subscribers, and EventBridge routes events.

refs.title: What is Amazon Simple Queue Service?

scenario: Which service sends notifications to many subscribers, such as email, SMS and Lambda, at once?
explanation: Amazon SNS uses publish/subscribe topics to send messages to many subscribers at once, such as email, SMS and Lambda. SQS is a queue holding messages for a consumer.

refs.title: What is Amazon Simple Queue Service?

scenario: Which service defines AWS infrastructure as code using templates?
explanation: AWS CloudFormation defines infrastructure as code in templates so stacks are repeatable. The AWS CDK lets you write those definitions in programming languages. Config and CloudTrail only record activity.

scenario: Which service helps manage and patch fleets of EC2 instances and on-premises servers?
explanation: AWS Systems Manager manages and patches fleets of EC2 instances and on-premises servers, with features such as Patch Manager, Session Manager and Run Command. Inspector only scans for vulnerabilities.

scenario: Which service queries data in S3 using standard SQL without loading it into a database?
explanation: Amazon Athena queries data in S3 with standard SQL without loading it into a database. It's serverless and charges per amount of data scanned.

scenario: Which service creates interactive business intelligence dashboards?
explanation: Amazon QuickSight (now part of Amazon Quick) builds interactive business intelligence dashboards from sources such as Athena, Redshift and RDS. Athena only queries.

scenario: Which service collects and processes real-time streaming data, such as clickstreams?
explanation: Amazon Kinesis collects and processes real-time streaming data such as clickstreams. Athena and Redshift analyze stored data, and Glue prepares and catalogs it.

refs.title: What is Amazon Kinesis Data Streams?

scenario: Which service lets developers build and train their own machine learning models?
explanation: Amazon SageMaker AI is for building, training and deploying your own machine learning models. Rekognition, Polly and Translate are pre-built AI services needing no ML expertise.

scenario: Which service analyzes images and videos to detect objects and faces?
explanation: Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and video to detect objects, faces and text. Comprehend analyzes text, Textract extracts text from documents and Lex builds chatbots.

scenario: Which service gives access to foundation models from several providers through one API for generative AI apps?
explanation: Amazon Bedrock offers foundation models from several providers through one API for building generative AI applications. Rekognition and Polly are task-specific AI services.

scenario: A workload runs steadily 24/7 for the next three years. Which EC2 pricing option is typically cheapest?
explanation: For steady 24/7 use over one to three years, Reserved Instances or Savings Plans are typically cheapest, with discounts up to about 72% versus On-Demand. Spot can be interrupted.

scenario: A batch job can be stopped and restarted at any time. Which EC2 option offers the biggest discount?
explanation: Spot Instances use spare capacity at up to about 90% off and can be interrupted with a two-minute notice, so they suit batch jobs that can stop and restart.

scenario: A team is testing a new app for a few weeks and doesn't know how long it'll run. Which pricing option fits?
explanation: On-Demand has no commitment, so it suits short or unpredictable use such as a few weeks of testing. A 3-year commitment is wasteful for something that may end soon.

scenario: Which pricing option commits to a dollar amount per hour of compute and applies to EC2, Fargate and Lambda?
explanation: Compute Savings Plans commit to a dollar amount per hour and apply across EC2, Fargate and Lambda, flexible across instance families and Regions. Standard Reserved Instances are tied to specific instances.

scenario: A company must use its existing per-socket software licenses on physical servers. Which option fits?
explanation: Dedicated Hosts give a physical server dedicated to you with visibility into sockets and cores, which supports per-socket software licensing. Spot and Lambda can't.

scenario: Which is generally free in AWS?

options.text: Data transfer into AWS from the internet
Data transfer out to the internet

explanation: Data transfer into AWS from the internet is generally free. Data transfer out, EBS storage and NAT gateway hours are charged.

scenario: Which tool estimates the cost of a planned AWS architecture before deployment?
explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of a planned architecture before deployment, and estimates can be shared. Cost Explorer and Budgets work on actual spend.

scenario: Which tool visualizes past AWS spending and forecasts future costs?
explanation: AWS Cost Explorer visualizes past spending and forecasts future costs, filterable by service, account and tag. Pricing Calculator estimates a planned design.

refs.title: Analyzing your costs and usage with AWS Cost Explorer

scenario: A company wants an email alert when monthly spend is forecast to exceed $1,000. What should it use?
explanation: AWS Budgets can alert you when actual or forecasted spend crosses a threshold, and can trigger actions. Cost Explorer analyzes but doesn't alert on thresholds.

refs.title: Managing your costs with AWS Budgets

scenario: Which feature helps track costs by project or department?
explanation: Cost allocation tags label resources by project or department; activate them in the Billing console to see costs grouped by tag in reports.

refs.title: Organizing and tracking costs using AWS cost allocation tags

scenario: Which feature gives a single bill for many AWS accounts and can combine usage for volume discounts?
explanation: Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations combines accounts into one bill and can pool usage for volume discounts, sharing Reserved Instance and Savings Plans benefits.

scenario: Which tool provides the most detailed, line-item cost and usage data for analysis?

options.text: AWS Cost and Usage Reports (Data Exports)

explanation: AWS Cost and Usage Reports (Data Exports) provide the most detailed line-item cost data, delivered to S3 and queryable with Athena. Pricing Calculator produces estimates only.

refs.title: Analyzing your costs and usage with AWS Cost Explorer

scenario: Which service recommends right-sized EC2 instances based on usage history?
explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer recommends right-sized resources, such as EC2 instances, from usage history. Artifact, Macie and Shield don't analyze utilization.

scenario: Which service checks an account for cost savings, security gaps, fault tolerance and service limits?
explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor checks an account for cost optimization, security, fault tolerance, performance and service limits. Basic Support includes core checks; paid plans unlock the full set.

scenario: Which AWS Support plan is free for every account?
explanation: Basic Support is included free with every account. It covers billing and account support, documentation, re:Post, the Health Dashboard and core Trusted Advisor checks.

scenario: Which AWS Support plan includes a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM)?
explanation: A designated Technical Account Manager comes with Enterprise Support, not Basic. The plan names and tiers have changed, so check the current plans page.

scenario: Which resource offers free answers to AWS questions from the community and AWS experts?
explanation: AWS re:Post offers free answers from the community and AWS experts. Marketplace sells software and Artifact provides compliance reports.

scenario: Where can a customer buy third-party software, such as firewalls, that runs on AWS?
explanation: AWS Marketplace is the catalog for buying third-party software such as firewalls that runs on AWS, with free trials and hourly or annual pricing.

scenario: A company needs help from a consulting firm to migrate to AWS. Which program helps find one?
explanation: The AWS Partner Network (APN) helps customers find consulting and technology partners. AWS Professional Services is AWS's own consulting team.

scenario: Which shows the status of AWS services and events that affect a customer's own resources?
explanation: The AWS Health Dashboard shows service status and personalized alerts about events, maintenance and outages affecting your own resources.

scenario: Who should a customer contact for help with a billing question?
explanation: Account and billing support cases are available on every support plan, including Basic, so contact AWS Support. Marketplace sellers and Artifact don't handle billing.

scenario: Which factor affects Amazon S3 storage costs?

options.text: The number of VPCs in the account

explanation: S3 costs depend on storage class and amount stored, plus requests and data transfer out. IAM user count, VPC count and console language don't affect it.

refs.title: Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes

scenario: What's the main cost benefit of turning off development EC2 instances outside working hours?

options.text: You stop paying for compute while stopped

explanation: Stopping dev instances outside working hours stops compute charges, though EBS volumes and unattached Elastic IPs still cost. Instance Scheduler on AWS can automate start and stop.

scenario: Which pricing option needs no commitment but can be reclaimed by AWS with a two-minute warning?
explanation: Spot Instances need no commitment but AWS can reclaim them with a two-minute warning, so use them for fault-tolerant, flexible workloads. On-Demand and Savings Plans aren't reclaimed.
